S4. Complaints
S4.1 A complaint is an expression of dissatisfaction with Pacify's service, as distinct from a request for
information or a transaction.
S4.2 Complaints are acknowledged within 24 hours and resolved within 7 business days.
S4.3 A complaint is not required to be framed as a complaint to be treated as one. Where a customer expresses
dissatisfaction in the course of another enquiry, a complaint record is opened.
S4.4 The response to a complaint must address the substance of the dissatisfaction. A restatement of the policy
that gave rise to the complaint is not a response.
S4.5 Where a complaint is upheld, the remedy may include correction of the underlying matter, an apology,
store credit, or waiver of a fee. Where it is not upheld, the customer is given reasons and informed of the right to
escalate under S3.
title: Customer Service Policy

S5.1 In accordance with applicable consumer protection requirements, Pacify designates a Grievance Officer.
S5.2 Grievance Officer: Ms. R. Iyer, grievance@pacify.com. Written correspondence may be addressed to the
registered office.
S5.3 The Grievance Officer responds within 7 days of receipt and disposes of the grievance within 30 days.
S5.4 A customer is not required to exhaust S3 before approaching the Grievance Officer, but is ordinarily better
served by doing so.

S8. Personal data
S8.1 Pacify retains order records for 7 years in accordance with tax requirements, and interaction records for 3
years.
S8.2 A customer may request a copy of their personal data. The request is fulfilled within 30 days, subject to
verification under S6.
S8.3 A customer may request deletion of their personal data. Deletion is completed within 30 days, save that:
(a) order and invoice records subject to the retention period at S8.1 are retained;
(b) where a return, refund, warranty claim, or complaint is open, deletion is deferred until it is closed;

matter is open.

title: Customer Service Policy

S10. Conduct
S10.1 Pacify staff will not be abusive, dismissive, or misleading, and will not argue with a customer.
S10.2 Where a customer is abusive, uses discriminatory language, or makes a threat against an individual, the
interaction may be terminated after one warning. The underlying matter continues to be dealt with in writing.
S10.3 Frustration, anger, and forceful language directed at Pacify as an organisation are not grounds for
terminating an interaction.
title: Customer Service Policy

S11.1 Chat transcripts and call recordings are retained for 3 years for quality and training purposes.
S11.2 A customer may request a copy of a transcript or recording of their own interaction, subject to S6.

S12.1 Pacify uses an automated assistant to provide first-line support at all hours. S12.2 Where a customer asks whether they are communicating with a person or with an automated system, the

told when a human agent will respond. EU Regional Addendum
Document reference: POL-EU-001
Version: 1.1
Effective from: 15 January 2026
Applies to: Customers resident in the European Union member states listed at POL-SHP-001 S1.2

title: EU Regional Addendum

text:
S1. Status of this Addendum
S1.1 This Addendum supplements the Returns Policy (POL-RET-002) and the Refunds Policy (POL-REF-001)
in respect of customers resident in the European Union.
S1.2 Where this Addendum conflicts with POL-RET-002 or POL-REF-001, this Addendum prevails. The
provisions of those Policies continue to apply to the extent that they are not displaced.
S1.3 This Addendum reflects rights conferred by European Union consumer law. Those rights cannot be
excluded, limited, or made subject to conditions by Pacify.
title: EU Regional Addendum

text:
S2. Right of withdrawal
S2.1 A customer resident in the European Union may withdraw from a contract of sale within 14 calendar days
of taking physical possession of the goods. S2.2 No reason need be given. Pacify may not ask for a reason as a condition of accepting the withdrawal,
and may not decline a withdrawal on the basis of the reason given. S2.3 The right of withdrawal applies whether or not the item has been opened. The distinction drawn at
POL-RET-002 S2.1 and S3 between opened and unopened items has no application to EU customers, and
neither the 30-day nor the 14-day window in that Policy applies. The single applicable period is the 14 days at
S2.1. S2.4 A customer may inspect and test the goods to the extent necessary to establish their nature,
characteristics, and functioning, in the manner that would be permitted in a physical shop.
title: EU Regional Addendum

text:
S2.4 A customer may inspect and test the goods to the extent necessary to establish their nature,
characteristics, and functioning, in the manner that would be permitted in a physical shop. Doing so does not
affect the right of withdrawal. S2.5 Where a customer has handled the goods beyond what S2.4 permits, Pacify may reduce the
reimbursement to reflect any diminished value. Any such reduction must be justified and communicated with
reasons.
title: EU Regional Addendum

text:
S3. Exercising the right
S3.1 Withdrawal is exercised by an unambiguous statement to that effect, sent to support@pacify.com or
through the customer's Pacify account. No prescribed form is required.
S3.2 The 14-day period at S2.1 is satisfied if the statement is sent before the period expires. The goods need
not have been despatched within it.
S3.3 The customer must return the goods within 14 calendar days of giving notice of withdrawal.
title: EU Regional Addendum

text:
S4.1 No restocking fee may be applied to a return effected under this Addendum. POL-RET-002 S10 does
not apply.
S4.2 The customer bears the direct cost of returning the goods, unless the goods are defective, damaged on
arrival, or not as described, in which case Pacify bears it.
S4.3 The fixed return shipping contribution at POL-RET-002 S9.1 does not apply. The customer arranges return
carriage and bears the actual cost.
S4.4 Pacify reimburses the standard outbound delivery charge paid by the customer. Where the customer
elected an enhanced delivery method, only the standard charge is reimbursed.
title: EU Regional Addendum

text:
S5. Reimbursement
S5.1 Pacify reimburses all sums received from the customer, subject to S4, within 14 calendar days of the
earlier of:
(a) the date Pacify receives the returned goods; or
(b) the date the customer supplies evidence of having despatched them.
S5.2 The period at S5.1 displaces the processing periods at POL-REF-001 S3 where the latter would be longer.
S5.3 Reimbursement is made using the same means of payment used for the original transaction, unless the
customer expressly agrees otherwise.
title: EU Regional Addendum

text:
S6. Exceptions to the right of withdrawal
S6.1 The right of withdrawal does not apply to:
(a) goods made to the customer's specifications or clearly personalised;
(b) sealed software, audio, or video recordings where the seal has been broken;
(c) sealed goods which are not suitable for return for reasons of health protection or hygiene, where the seal has
been broken after delivery.
S6.2 The exclusions at POL-RET-002 S5.1 apply only insofar as they correspond to S6.1. In particular, the
exclusion of custom-configured units at POL-RET-002 S5.1(d) corresponds to S6.1(a) and is effective; the
exclusion of consumables at POL-RET-002 S5.1(e) has no corresponding basis and is not effective against EU
customers.
section_title: Exceptions to the right of withdrawal
title: EU Regional Addendum

text:
S7. Statutory guarantee of conformity
S7.1 In addition to the right of withdrawal, EU customers benefit from a statutory guarantee that goods conform
to the contract for a period of two years from delivery.
S7.2 The statutory guarantee operates alongside the Warranty Policy (POL-WAR-001) and is not displaced by
it. Where the Warranty Policy provides a shorter period, the statutory period nevertheless applies.
S7.3 For the first twelve months, a defect is presumed to have existed at delivery unless Pacify proves
otherwise.
title: EU Regional Addendum

text:
S8. Dispute resolution
S8.1 EU customers may refer an unresolved dispute to the alternative dispute resolution body in their member
state, or to the European Online Dispute Resolution platform.
S8.2 Referral under S8.1 does not require prior exhaustion of the escalation procedure at POL-CS-001 S3.
title: EU Regional Addendum

S2. Equated monthly instalments
S2.1 EMI is available on orders of Rs 15,000 and above. S2.2 Available tenures are 3, 6, 9, 12, 18, and 24 months. Availability of a given tenure depends on the issuing
bank. S2.3 EMI is available on credit cards from participating banks and, for certain banks, on debit cards subject to
the bank's own eligibility assessment. S2.4 Interest is set by the issuing bank and not by Pacify. The rate applicable is displayed at checkout before
confirmation. S2.5 Where an offer is described as "no-cost EMI", the interest chargeable by the bank is absorbed by Pacify
and applied as a discount to the item price at the point of sale. The customer is charged instalments totalling the
original price, of which a portion represents bank interest funded by that discount. S2.6 The consequence of S2.5 on a return is dealt with at POL-REF-001 S7.3.
title: Payments Policy

text:

discounted amount actually paid, and the absorbed interest is not returned to the customer. S2.7 A processing fee may be levied by the issuing bank on EMI conversion. Such fee is not refundable by
Pacify.
title: Payments Policy

text:
S3. Cash on delivery
S3.1 Cash on delivery is available on orders up to Rs 50,000 in value.
title: Payments Policy

text:
S3.2 A handling fee of Rs 50 applies to every cash on delivery order. The fee is not refundable in any
circumstances, including where the order is returned.
S3.3 Cash on delivery is not available at restricted pincodes identified under POL-SHP-001 S1.4, nor for
made-to-order items, nor for orders including a gift card.
S3.4 The carrier accepts cash and, at most delivery locations, card and UPI payment on the doorstep.
S3.5 Refund of a cash on delivery order requires bank details from the customer. See POL-REF-001 S8.

text:
S4. Failed payments and automatic reversal
S4.1 A payment may fail for reasons including insufficient funds, an expired card, a declined authentication, a
bank-side timeout, or a gateway timeout. S4.2 Where a payment fails, no order is created. The customer may retry immediately using the same or a
different method. S4.3 In some failure modes the customer's bank places a hold on the funds, or debits and then must reverse the
amount. Where this occurs, the amount is automatically reversed by the bank within 5 to 7 business days. No action by the customer or by Pacify is required, and Pacify cannot accelerate the reversal because Pacify
never received the funds. S4.4 The reversal at S4.3 is not a refund. A refund arises only where an order was completed and subsequently
returned, and is governed by POL-REF-001. Customers frequently conflate the two. The distinguishing question
is whether an order reference exists:

A refund arises only where an order was completed and subsequently
returned, and is governed by POL-REF-001. Customers frequently conflate the two. The distinguishing question
is whether an order reference exists: if no order was created, the matter is a reversal under this section. S4.5 Where an amount has not been reversed after 7 business days, the customer should raise the matter with
their bank quoting the transaction reference, and notify Pacify so that the gateway record can be supplied in
support.

text:
S5. Double charges
S5.1 A double charge arises where two settled transactions correspond to a single order.
S5.2 On report, Pacify verifies against gateway records within 2 business days.
S5.3 Where a double charge is confirmed, the duplicate is refunded within 7 to 10 business days of

Do I need an account to buy something?
Yes. You need an account so we can show you your order status, handle returns, and keep your invoices in one

redirect it. You cannot swap items on an existing order — cancel it and place a new one. Can I cancel an order?

No. All orders go through the website or the app. Do you keep my card details?

Yes, unless the listing says "refurbished". Refurbished units are clearly marked and come with a 6-month

What is the difference between a Pacify-branded product and the other brands you sell?
Two things. Pacify hardware carries 24 months of warranty rather than 12. And if something goes wrong with a
Pacify product, we handle the whole repair ourselves. For other brands, the warranty is the manufacturer's and
you deal with their service network — we can point you to the nearest centre and confirm your purchase date,
but we cannot authorise a repair on their behalf.

Two weeks from the day it arrives, if you have opened it. A month if the seal is still intact. Accessories get a

Pacify — Technical Support Guide

Last updated: 15 January 2026
Work through the section that matches your symptom. If a step asks you to power the
device off, do that properly rather than closing the lid.
title: Technical Support Guide

text:
S1. Before you start
S1.1 Back up anything you cannot lose. Several steps in this guide, particularly S11, will erase data.
S1.2 Note down any error code you can see, exactly as displayed. Codes are the fastest route to a diagnosis,
and S9 lists what each one means.
S1.3 If your device is brand new and has arrived faulty, stop here and report it within 48 hours instead of
troubleshooting. That route gets you a free replacement and no fees. See POL-RET-002 S6.
S1.4 It is fine to unbox a new device and switch it on to check it works. Doing so does not stop you returning it,
though note that once the retail seal is broken the item counts as opened for the purposes of the return window.
S1.5 Use the charger that came in the box. A large share of the faults reported to us turn out to be a third-party
charger.
title: Technical Support Guide

text:
S2. Will not power on
S2.1 Hold the power button for 15 seconds, release, then press once.
S2.2 Connect the supplied charger and leave it for 30 minutes. A fully depleted battery will not respond
immediately.
S2.3 Check the charger light. No light means the charger or the wall socket. Try a different socket.
S2.4 On the ProBook range, hold power plus volume-down for 20 seconds to force a hardware reset.
S2.5 If you see a light or hear a fan but the screen stays dark, that is a display fault, not a power fault. Go to S3.
S2.6 If none of this produces a response, the unit needs service. Raise a warranty claim under POL-WAR-001
S10.
title: Technical Support Guide

text:
S3. Display problems
S3.1 Screen is black but the device is running. Connect an external monitor. If the external picture is fine, the
panel or its cable has failed and needs service. S3.2 Screen flickers. Update the display driver first. If flicker persists across a driver reinstall and appears on
the login screen as well, it is hardware. S3.3 Screen goes dark intermittently on an external monitor. This is usually a cable or handshake problem
rather than a panel fault. Reseat both ends of the cable, try a different cable, and check for a monitor firmware
update. Code ERR-DP-0x004 confirms this diagnosis. S3.4 Picture is there but the wrong size or refresh rate. Check the display settings match the panel's native
resolution. Code ERR-DP-0x011 means the rate you have selected is not supported over the cable in use. S3.5 Dead or stuck pixels. Count them against a full-screen test at black, white, red, green, and blue.
title: Technical Support Guide

text:
S3.5 Dead or stuck pixels. Count them against a full-screen test at black, white, red, green, and blue. Five or
more is covered under warranty; fewer than five is not. See POL-WAR-001 S6. S3.6 Backlight is uneven or has gone entirely. Covered regardless of pixel count. Code DSP-014 indicates
backlight failure.
title: Technical Support Guide

text:
S4. Battery and charging
S4.1 Not charging. Try a different socket, then check the cable for damage. Code BAT-042 means the charger
is not being recognised, which is usually the cable.
S4.2 Drains quickly. Check which applications are consuming power in the system settings. A background
sync or an indexing job will flatten a battery in an afternoon.
S4.3 Check the health figure. Open Pacify Diagnostics and read the maximum capacity percentage. Below
80% inside the first 12 months is a warranty matter. Above 80%, or beyond 12 months, is normal wear.
S4.4 Code BAT-119 means capacity has fallen below 60%. That is a warranty replacement if the device is under
12 months old — do not attempt further troubleshooting.
S4.5 Swollen battery or a device that will not sit flat. Stop using it immediately, unplug it, and contact us. Do
not charge it.
title: Technical Support Guide

text:
S5. Wi-Fi and connectivity
S5.1 Toggle Wi-Fi off and on, then restart the device.
S5.2 Forget the network and rejoin it, entering the password afresh.
S5.3 Restart the router. Two thirds of connectivity reports resolve here.
S5.4 Code WIFI-503 means the wireless driver failed to initialise. Reinstall the driver from the Pacify support
site. If it recurs after a clean reinstall, the wireless module needs service.
S5.5 Connects but no internet. The problem is the network, not the device. Test with a phone hotspot to
confirm.
S5.6 Bluetooth will not pair. Remove the existing pairing on both devices and start over. Bluetooth and Wi-Fi
share an antenna on the ProBook 14 Lite, so a heavily congested 2.4 GHz environment can affect both.
title: Technical Support Guide

text:
S6. Audio
S6.1 Check the output device selection first. A previously paired headset will silently claim the output.
S6.2 Code AUD-330 indicates a driver conflict, usually after installing third-party audio software. Uninstall it and
reinstall the Pacify audio driver.
S6.3 One earbud silent on SoundPods. Place both in the case, close it for 10 seconds, reopen. If it persists,
reset by holding both stems for 15 seconds.
S6.4 Crackling on the internal speakers at high volume is distortion, not a fault, unless it is present at
moderate volume too.
title: Technical Support Guide

text:
S7. Performance and heat
S7.1 Check for a runaway process in the task manager before anything else.
S7.2 Confirm the vents are clear. A laptop used on bedding will throttle within minutes.
S7.3 Code THRM-88 means the device has been throttling under sustained thermal load. That is protective
behaviour, not a fault, unless it occurs at idle.
S7.4 Storage above 90% full will slow the whole system noticeably. Clear space and re-test.
S7.5 Run the Pacify Diagnostics full hardware test. It reports storage health, memory errors, and fan behaviour.
title: Technical Support Guide

text:
S8. Software and drivers
S8.1 Install pending operating system updates before reporting any software symptom.
S8.2 Drivers are on the Pacify support site under your model. Do not install drivers sourced elsewhere.
S8.3 Note that software faults, operating system errors, driver conflicts, and data loss are excluded from
warranty cover under POL-WAR-001 S3.1(f). We will still help you troubleshoot them, but they are not a
hardware claim.
S8.4 Installing a different operating system does not void your hardware warranty. Faults caused by it are not
covered, but the hardware remains covered.
title: Technical Support Guide

S10.1 Test the peripheral on a second device before assuming the port has failed.

S11.2 From the operating system, use the built-in reset option and choose whether to keep files.

S5. Battery coverage
S5.1 A battery is covered where its measured maximum capacity falls below 80% of its rated capacity within
12 months of delivery, under a cycle count consistent with normal use.
S5.2 Capacity is measured using the Pacify Diagnostics application or the manufacturer's equivalent utility. A
reading obtained by third-party software is not accepted.
S5.3 A battery reporting error code BAT-119 has, by definition, fallen below 60% capacity and is covered if
within the period at S5.1.
S5.4 Capacity loss above 80%, and capacity loss of any degree after 12 months, is normal wear and is not
covered. Replacement is available as a paid service.

S6. Display and pixel defects
S6.1 A display is covered where it exhibits 5 or more dead, stuck, or permanently lit sub-pixels within the
warranty period.
S6.2 A display exhibiting fewer than 5 such pixels does not meet the threshold and is not covered. This
threshold reflects panel manufacturing tolerances applied across the industry and is not subject to negotiation or
to discretionary exception by support staff.

and blue.

discolouration, persistent flicker, visible bleed exceeding 10% of screen area, and complete panel failure. Error
code DSP-014 indicates backlight failure and is covered.
